notes: 133 BCE is a periodisation boundary (Tiberius Gracchus' tribunate and killing); Senate and magistracies continued unbroken. Q4: Sicilian slave revolt 135-132 BCE (c.70,000 slaves) counts as large revolt.

successor: French Kingdom - Late Valois (same Valois monarchy)
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Charles VII, king of France' - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Charles-VII-king-of-France
notes: 1450 is a period boundary; Valois monarchy ruled 1328-1589 without break. Q4: Armagnac-Burgundian civil war (1407-35); English held Paris 1420-36 but Charles VII's apparatus survived and recovered it; Praguerie revolt 1440.

Justinian's Gothic War (535-c.554) destroyed the kingdom; Belisarius took the capital Ravenna in 540, which became the Byzantine exarchate seat; Totila killed at Taginae 552. Q4: noble plots, Amalasuntha murdered 535, Theodahad deposed 536.

Pippinid mayors ruled de facto since Tertry 687; in 751 Pippin III deposed Childeric III and was elected king: dynastic change within the same Frankish apparatus. Q4: 714-19 succession civil war, 740s revolts. 'Paris' capital questionable.

source2: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, 'Empires of the Western Sudan: Mali Empire' - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/mali/hd_mali.htm
notes: 1410 is not an ending: Mali persisted in its Upper Niger heartland, losing Gao (revolt c.1400) and Timbuktu/Walata (1431); politically minor by c.1550, shrunk to original territory by 1645. Database end date looks arbitrary.

successor: Timurid Empire (Ulus Chaghatay under Timurid amirs)
source2: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, 'The Art of the Timurid Period (ca. 1370-1507)' - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/timu/hd_timu.htm
notes: From 1340s tribal amirs ruled Transoxiana through figurehead khans; Timur, a local tribal insider, became virtual ruler 1370 and kept nominal khans to c.1448, so 1402 is no break. Alternative reading: T1c. Q4: amir wars, Moghul invasions.

Onin War broke Ashikaga power; shogun a figurehead amid daimyo fragmentation. Owari daimyo Nobunaga (internal) entered Kyoto 1568 with puppet shogun Yoshiaki, exiling him 1573, ending the shogunate. Database end 1568; authority ended 1573.

source2: Internet Encyclopedia of Ukraine (Canadian Institute of Ukrainian Studies), 'Mongols' - http://www.encyclopediaofukraine.com/display.asp?linkpath=pages%5CM%5CO%5CMongols.htm
notes: Rus fragmented amid princely infighting; Mongols conquered Rus 1239-41, storming and destroying Kyiv in 1240, then held hegemony via the Golden Horde. Listed candidates wrong: Lithuania took Kyiv only in 1362. No capital listed; Kyiv assumed.

Core Kuching = Sarawak: Brooke Raj 1841, Japanese occupation 1942-45 (reversed), crown colony 1946, joined Malaysia by negotiated agreement 1963 (T3 arguable). Database end 1987 looks wrong. Q4: anti-cession unrest, 1962 Brunei revolt reached Limbang.

Yellow Turban revolt (184), Dong Zhuo's 189-190 seizure and burning of Luoyang split the empire among rival generals; Cao Cao, a Han official, controlled the emperor from 196; Xiandi ceded throne to Cao Pi 220. No external conquest.
